subject: Clarify: default capture & deletion windows for requests, responses, and generated outputs
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@crescentfin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: questions on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Mina / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. Our security team put together a quick questionnaire (attached) to confirm the default behavior for logs and outputs before we sign the DPA amendment. High-level items we need clarified:

- By default, how long are raw requests (user prompts / payloads) retained?
- How long are model responses / generated outputs stored?
- Is streaming token data treated differently from final outputs?
- Are there any backup or snapshot retention windows customers should be aware of (for regulatory eDiscovery)?
- If we ask for a full customer erase, what evidence/proof do you provide and how long does that process take?

Can you also note whether any of these defaults are region-dependent (US vs EU) or change when customers choose "Private" deployment?

I've attached our questionnaire (crescent_questionnaire_v1.xlsx). Appreciate a short written reply we can share with legal; we can follow with a 30-min call if needed.

Best,
Alyssa
Sr. Security Program Manager
Crescent Financial

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@crescentfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-21T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: questions on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Below is a concise summary you can share with legal. I tried to keep answers short and actionable; happy to jump on a call to walk through any items.

Summary of Redwood default capture (hosted API, US regions):
- Raw request payloads (prompts / input fields): retained by default for 30 days. These are the records accepted by our ingestion layer.
- Model responses / final outputs: retained by default for 90 days for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Streaming token buffers: transient. Tokens emitted during a streaming session are kept in in-memory buffers and short-lived logs for up to 2 hours for session recovery; they are not persisted to long-term storage unless explicitly captured by a customer-level debug flag.
- KV cache / session caches: ephemeral; typical TTL is 1 hour and subject to eviction based on memory pressure.
- Backups & snapshots: snapshots of telemetry and infrastructure logs (not customer prompt/response stores) may be kept for up to 180 days for disaster recovery; completeness/exceptions described below.

Erase & evidence process:
- Customer-initiated full erase: we perform data removal from primary stores within 7 business days after a validated request.
- Proof of deletion: we provide a deletion report and scoped evidence (record ids, timestamps, runbook steps) within 10 business days.
- Note: backups or archived snapshots that contain data may require additional time to scrub (up to 90 days) depending on the retention tier. We provide an attestation of the scrub schedule and expected completion window in those cases.

Region / deployment notes:
- EU residency: hosted EU regions will keep default windows consistent unless a customer has opted for a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) where retention controls and TTLs are customer-managed.
- Private deployments: when customers run Redwood Private with customer-managed storage, Redwood does not control retention TTLs unless explicitly contracted.

Opt-outs & flags:
- Customers can opt out of default capture using the no_store/no_log API flag (or equivalent field in SDKs). When used correctly, this prevents persistent storage of the request/response pair beyond immediate processing and ephemeral debugging buffers.
- There are limited exceptions where we may retain minimal metadata for billing and abuse detection (timestamp, request-size, model-id) for the billing window; these are aggregated and cannot be used to reconstruct prompt text.

Next steps:
- If Crescent wants custom retention windows or faster purge SLAs, we can include those in the contract amendment (typical enterprise add-on).
- I can draft a short one-page runbook tailored to Crescent that your legal team can attach to the DPA.

Attached: redline_sample_dpa.pdf (sample language for retention windows and erasure evidence).

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@crescentfin.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: questions on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Alyssa / team — adding a legal perspective and one small clarifying point for the DPA:

- "Prompts" vs "generated outputs": For contract language we prefer to distinguish "customer-submitted input" (the full payload) from "derived outputs" (model responses). Both are covered by our erasure process, but the runbook will call out precise record keys and the expected proof artifacts (run id, deletion job id, list of record keys removed).
- NO_LOG / no_store flag: important to note this only applies to persistent storage; telemetry and minimal billing metadata may still exist for the billing reconciliation window. We typically exclude that metadata from erasure requests unless specifically requested.
- Exceptions: legal hold or regulatory preservation requests override the immediate purge; in those cases we provide the customer with the retention justification and the legal contact that opened the hold.

If Crescent legal would like to propose specific redlines to the sample DPA language I attached, send them over and we can do a marked-up pass.

-Kim
General Counsel (acting), Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@crescentfin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-22T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: questions on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Thanks Mina / Kim — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from our side after reviewing internally:

1) Can you confirm the deletion evidence format? Our auditors need: record IDs removed, UTC timestamps, the deletion job id, and a signed attestation from Redwood. Is that something you can produce?
2) For the EU option: if we select hosted EU region (not Private), do the default windows (30 / 90 / 2hr) remain the same? We are evaluating whether to ask for Private to control retention.
3) Are there any limits on retention exceptions for backups that would prevent us from meeting a regulator's 30-day erase request?

We'd prefer a short call to align; can Mina / Kim do 30 min Thurs or Friday afternoon PST?

Best,
Alyssa

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@crescentfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-23T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: questions on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Alyssa — quick answers and a proposed runbook attachable to the DPA:

1) Deletion evidence: yes, we provide a standard deletion package that includes
   - list of record IDs removed (CSV),
   - deletion job id(s) and UTC timestamps,
   - a signed attestation from Redwood with signatory name and role,
   - a short summary of the scrub scope (primary stores + expected snapshot scrub schedule).
   Target delivery: evidence within 10 business days of a validated erase request.

2) EU hosted region parity: default retention windows in our EU-hosted regions are the same as US-hosted defaults (30d requests / 90d outputs / 2hr stream buffer) unless explicitly updated in contract. The difference is residency of stored data; records remain in-region and subject to local export controls.

3) Backups & regulator 30-day requests: backups can extend the timeline. Our standard backup scrub approach is: primary store purge within 7 business days; archive snapshot scrub scheduled and completed within 90 days. If Crescent must comply with a regulator requiring strict 30-day absolute deletion, we recommend: (a) Private deployment with customer-managed storage, or (b) a contract addendum that imposes accelerated backup scrub windows + dedicated deletion confirmation flow.

Next steps:
- I will prepare a one-page runbook for Crescent with the exact evidence template and sample attestation. Marissa will help produce the exact CSV headers that auditors expect.
- Proposed call: Friday 2029-04-26 at 1:00pm PST. If that works, we'll send an invite.

Thanks — Mina
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

On a related note, Marissa: when you have the CSV headers and the attestation template, please drop them into the SEC-4821 ticket and I will forward to Crescent before the call.
